correctness.rationale: The positive periodic kernel solves (L_cycle+2I)h=2δ_0, sums to one, and has total variation 2(a−b). A rung source is antisymmetric. At a rim source the two layer gradients split into A_i and D_i, with A_i=δ_i0−1/n and D_i=δ_i0−h_i. The two absolute rail drops add to max(|A_i|,|D_i|); a>1/n and the rung variation give precisely q_R. The two diagonal corrections give both c columns. Graph automorphisms leave only two orbits and symmetry equates the endpoints. A separate exact calculation checks all n=3,…,11 orbit-difference fractions. For n≥12 there are n−5 sites at distance at least three, with total mass <61/1000; summing (1/n−h_i)_+≥1/n−h_i there gives the bound used in both strict inequalities. The cut-minus-cycle rim difference is 1−1/n−a, strictly positive for n≥5 by decreasing a and a_5=11/19; n=3,4 were separately checked. Uniform geometric upper and lower bounds in cyclic distance give 2 log(n)/log(1/ρ)+O(1) non-source sites above threshold and O(1/n) mass outside them. Thus substituting the positive-part sum gives precisely both stated limits and their common logarithmic deficit.
residual_risks: The replay covers only finite sizes through 18; the tail bound and geometric threshold establish the unrestricted inequalities and asymptotics.

evidence: At m=2, the cylinder kernel and mean are R=h_prism/2 and t=1/(2n). Its W=sum|R−t| is exactly the prism t_n since the deviations sum to zero and the source is above the mean. With z=b_n/2 and R_0−z=(a_n−b_n)/2, A_H, A_V, B_H, B_V specialize to q_R,q_V,c_R,c_V. Its threshold argument also applies to the rim asymptotics and yields the same two constants and correction coefficient.

In the cylinder proof of rim dominance, the cut comparison uses m−3≥0 and a lower bound for h; this cannot be used at m=2 with the opposite sign. The cycle comparison uses m≥4 or m=3 explicitly. The precise finite signs for m=2 and the n=3,4 transition therefore require a separate calculation, not substitution of a dominating parameter.
Entrywise data give the four sums after absolute values; they do not, without further inequalities, decide the sharp finite winners.

originality.rationale: There is substantial equivalent coverage of components: Azimi–Farrokhi give the exact incidence-pseudoinverse data, the cube norms are known, and the same-day clique-cylinder derivation specializes to the four prism column-sum formulas and the coefficient of the logarithmic rim deficit. I do not count those as distinct facts. The distinct claim supported by the full finding is the finite prism norm classification by competing orbits: the broader record does not prove a rim-winner theorem at m=2, and its lower-bound proof of the two comparisons does not specialize. The all-size rim-versus-rung inequalities, their different triangular-prism winners, and strict finite cut–cycle ordering are not a statement or direct substitution of those sources. No discovery chronology is inferred from the same-day dates.

value.rationale: The prism is the simplest periodic two-layer network. Different winning edge types for the two complements at n=3, a precise tie at n=4, and strict rim maxima thereafter give a usable finite-size classification beyond known current entries or eventual asymptotics. Showing that the classification persists at every n≥5 requires comparison of the positive-part threshold and diagonal penalties, not merely naming the cut matrix or evaluating a resistance.
residual_risks: The result concerns specified canonical projections, not minimal projections or uniform estimates for greater cross-section widths.
